question: According to Lindeman's 10% law of energy transfer, how much energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next higher trophic level?
options: 50% is transferred to the next level
100% of the energy is conserved and transferred without loss
Only 0.1% reaches the consumer
An average of 10% of food energy is transferred, while roughly 90% is lost to metabolic processes and heat
explanation: An average of 10% of the food eaten is turned into the organism's own body and made available for the next level of consumers. Therefore, 10% can be taken as the average value for the amount of organic matter that reaches the next level.

question: Why do food chains in natural ecosystems rarely exceed 4 or 5 trophic levels?
options: Apex predators refuse to consume small herbivores
Top carnivores run out of oxygen in high altitudes
Because so little usable energy remains after 4 or 5 transfers (due to 90% loss at each step) that it cannot support another viable population
Solar radiation cannot penetrate beyond the forest canopy
explanation: Because energy decreases by 90% at each successive step, very little usable energy remains after four trophic levels. Hence, food chains generally consist of only three or four steps; tertiary consumers rarely have sufficient energy to sustain a fifth trophic level.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 13, Section 13.1.1 Food Chains and Webs

question: Which statement accurately describes the flow of energy through any food chain in an ecosystem?
options: Energy flows in closed circular cycles, returning completely to the Sun
The flow of energy is strictly unidirectional: from Sun to producers to consumers, and cannot flow backward
Energy flows from top carnivores back to green plants
Energy oscillates bidirectionally between herbivores and plants
explanation: The flow of energy in an ecosystem is unidirectional. The energy captured by autotrophs does not revert back to the Sun, and the energy passed to herbivores cannot return to autotrophs. As it moves progressively through trophic levels, it is unavailable to previous levels.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 13, Section 13.1.1 Food Chains and Webs

question: What is the phenomenon in which the concentration of a persistent, bioaccumulative pollutant such as DDT increases in organisms at successively higher trophic levels?
options: Eutrophication
Bio-accumulation breakdown
Biological Magnification (Biomagnification)
Thermal pollution
explanation: Biomagnification is the increase in concentration of a persistent pollutant in organisms at successively higher trophic levels. subtopic: Ecological Decomposers: Role in Nutrient Cycling
question: What critical ecological role is carried out by decomposers (bacteria and fungi) in an ecosystem?

They act as top predators controlling herbivore populations
They trap solar energy for primary consumers
They break down complex organic remains of dead plants and animals into simple inorganic substances that replenish soil nutrients
explanation: Decomposers break down complex organic substances into simple inorganic substances that go into the soil and are used up once more by the plants. In their absence, dead animal carcasses and plant litter would pile up indefinitely, halting nutrient recycling.

High-energy UV radiation splits molecular oxygen (O2) into free oxygen atoms (O), which then combine with molecular oxygen: O + O2 -> O3

subtopic: Digestive Anatomy: Herbivore vs Carnivore Intestinal Length
question: Why do herbivorous mammals (like deer and cows) possess a significantly longer small intestine than carnivorous predators (like tigers)?
options: Herbivores eat larger stones that require grinding space
Plant material, especially cellulose-rich food, is generally slower to process; a longer digestive tract provides more time for digestion and microbial fermentation
Carnivores absorb water exclusively through their stomach
Herbivores produce no digestive enzymes
explanation: Many herbivores have a longer digestive tract because plant material is relatively difficult and time-consuming to digest. Symbiotic microorganisms ferment cellulose; in ruminants much of this fermentation occurs in the rumen, not because the small intestine itself digests cellulose.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 13 & Chapter 5, Section 5.2.3 Nutrition in Human Beings

question: Why is the Pyramid of Energy ALWAYS upright in every ecosystem without exception?
options: Solar radiation falls downwards from the sky
Energy is lost at each successive trophic level as heat and metabolic work, so higher levels always possess less energy than lower levels
Top predators outnumber producers in biomass
Producers reproduce slower than carnivores
explanation: Because energy transfer between trophic levels is governed by the second law of thermodynamics (average 10% transfer efficiency, 90% lost), available energy decreases progressively from producers to top carnivores. Thus, an energy pyramid is always upright.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 13, Section 13.1.1 Food Chains and Webs
